homepage.question: Who can contact Oakdene?
homepage.answer: Anyone looking for support, information, guidance, or help finding the right next step can contact Oakdene.

homepage.question: Do I need a formal referral?
homepage.answer: Not always. Some supports may begin with a simple enquiry, while others may use a referral form.

homepage.question: Is there a cost for services?
homepage.answer: Most of our services are free. Some community services such as the Ladies Boutique involve a small gold coin donation. We will always be upfront about any cost.

homepage.question: Can Oakdene help me find another service?
homepage.answer: Yes. If Oakdene is not the right fit, we can help point you toward other services and supports in the community.

homepage.question: Are your services confidential?
homepage.answer: Yes. We treat everything you share with us in confidence, in line with Australian privacy requirements.

homepage.question: Do you offer support in other languages?
homepage.answer: Yes. We offer support in multiple languages. If you need an interpreter, please let us know when you contact us and we will arrange one for you.

items.question: Who can access Oakdene's services?
items.answer: Anyone facing challenges with addiction, hardship, homelessness, or other life pressures can contact us. You don't need to meet specific criteria — if you're going through a difficult time and want support, we're here.

items.question: Do I need a referral?
items.answer: Not always. Some services (like the Kitchen, Laundrette, and Boutique) are drop-in and don't need a referral. For counselling and the Life Choices program, a referral helps us understand your situation, but you can also refer yourself directly.

items.question: How do I make a referral?
items.answer: Use our online [referral form](/services/referral/) or call [(02) 8717 0999](tel:+61287170999). Referrals can come from the person seeking support, a family member, or a professional (GP, case worker, corrections officer, etc.).

items.question: How long does it take to hear back after I contact you?
items.answer: We aim to respond to all enquiries within 2 business days. If you need help urgently, please call us directly on [(02) 8717 0999](tel:+61287170999), or see our [Need Help Now page](/need-help-now/) for 24/7 crisis lines.

items.question: Is everything confidential?
items.answer: Yes. What you share with an Oakdene counsellor or staff member is confidential, with a few important exceptions we're required by law to disclose (serious risk of harm to yourself or others, subpoena, or child protection concerns). Your counsellor will explain this at your first session.

items.question: Is there a cost?
items.answer: Most Oakdene services are free. Some community services (like the Ladies Boutique) ask for a gold coin donation. We'll always be upfront about any cost before you start.

items.question: What kind of counselling do you offer?
items.answer: We offer individual counselling, gambling counselling (via Catholic Care), and group programs. Our counsellors have specialist training in addiction, recovery, trauma, and mental health.

items.question: How long are counselling sessions?
items.answer: Typically 50–60 minutes. Your counsellor will talk with you about frequency — weekly, fortnightly, or as needed.

items.question: What is the Life Choices Program?
items.answer: A 6-week group program focused on recovery, life skills, and peer connection. See the [Life Choices page](/services/life-choices-program/) for details.

items.question: What is the Outpatients Program?
items.answer: A structured rehabilitation program combining counselling, group sessions, 12-step support, and peer mentoring. See the [Outpatients Program page](/services/outpatients-program/) for details.

items.question: Do you offer support in languages other than English?
items.answer: Yes. Several of our staff speak languages other than English, and we can arrange an interpreter if you let us know when you contact us. Our AA / GA meetings include Spanish-speaking sessions.

items.question: When is the Kitchen open?
items.answer: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, 12pm–2pm. Free nutritious meals are available to eligible community members.

items.question: When is the Laundrette open?
items.answer: Tuesday to Thursday, 12pm–2:30pm (last entry 1pm). Washing, drying, and detergent are provided free.

items.question: Can I get food to take home?
items.answer: Yes. Staple Food Packs are available every Friday, 12pm–1pm.

items.question: What is the Ladies Boutique?
items.answer: A warm, private space offering quality clothing and salon services for women, by appointment. No woman is turned away due to financial difficulty.

items.question: Do I need to book?
items.answer: Most drop-in community services don't need a booking during open hours. Ladies Boutique and counselling are by appointment.

items.question: How do I apply to volunteer?
items.answer: Submit our [volunteer application form](/community-programs/volunteering/). We'll get back to you within 2 business days to arrange a brief conversation.

items.question: Do I need experience?
items.answer: No. We value willingness, reliability, and a caring approach more than prior experience. We'll support you in your role.

items.question: Can my workplace / team volunteer together?
items.answer: Yes — we offer structured corporate volunteering days. See the [Corporate Volunteering page](/community-programs/volunteering/corporate-volunteering/) or get in touch.

items.question: Will I need a police check?
items.answer: For some volunteer roles (especially those involving clients or children), yes. We'll discuss this during your application.

items.question: Where are you located?
items.answer: 29 Vine Street, Fairfield NSW 2165. Parking is available via the Fairfield RSL open-air car park at the corner of Vine and Bertha Streets.

items.question: What are your opening hours?
items.answer: The centre is open Monday to Friday during business hours. Individual services have their own hours — see the [Contact page](/contact/) for the full schedule.

items.question: Are you a registered charity?
items.answer: Yes. Oakdene House Foundation is a registered Australian charity with the ACNC. ABN 90 151 950 926.

items.question: Is Oakdene religiously affiliated?
items.answer: Oakdene's services are open to everyone regardless of religion, background, or beliefs.

items.question: How do you handle my personal information?
items.answer: See our [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy/). In short: we collect only what we need to support you, keep it secure, and don't share it without your consent except where required by law.

items.question: Can I see what information you hold about me?
items.answer: Yes — you can request access to your records at any time. Contact us at [admin@oakdenehouse.org.au](mailto:admin@oakdenehouse.org.au).
